To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-{e}^{-x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-x}(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(-{e}^{-x})\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-{e}^{-x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-x}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})(-{e}^{-x})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{1}{3}I.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I.$ We remember to add a constant of integration $C$ at the end.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}J \\ I & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}(\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{1}{3}I) \\ I & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{9}-\frac{1}{9}I \\ \frac{10}{9}I & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3{e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9} \\ I & =-\frac{{e}^{-x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))}{10}+C\end{aligned}
$$
